first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, while two inherited findings indicate that reducing signup friction and shortening onboarding improved activation, completion, and time-to-value. This is better aligned with sustainable qualified revenue than promotional pricing, which carries a known retention penalty.

final.rationale: Run a targeted simplification experiment for SMB/simple-workspace accounts only, explicitly excluding complex workspaces. The verified evidence directly addresses the current onboarding and activation declines and showed qualified-revenue gains, but also revealed slight 30-day retention deterioration and materially higher churn when complex accounts received shortened onboarding. Guardrails should include retention, churn, and qualified revenue—not completion alone.
